Fast, reliable, and secure dependency management.

--- Yarn is a modern package manager split into various packages. Its novel architecture allows to do things currently impossible with existing solutions: - Yarn supports [plugins](https://yarnpkg.com/features/extensibility); adding a plugin is as simple as adding it into your repository - Yarn supports Node by default but isn't limited to it - plugins can add support for other languages - Yarn supports [workspaces](https://yarnpkg.com/features/workspaces) natively, and its CLI takes advantage of that - Yarn uses a bash-like [portable shell](https://github.com/yarnpkg/berry/tree/master/packages/yarnpkg-shell#yarnpkgshell) to make package scripts portable across Windows, Linux, and macOS - Yarn is first and foremost a [Node API](https://yarnpkg.com/api/) that can be used programmatically (via [@yarnpkg/core](packages/yarnpkg-core)) - Yarn is written in [TypeScript](https://www.typescriptlang.org/) and is fully type-checked ## Our supports ### [Gold sponsors](https://opencollective.com/yarnpkg)
All your environment variables, in one place. Stop struggling with scattered API keys, hacking together home-brewed tools, and avoiding access controls. Keep your team and servers in sync with Doppler.
Your app, enterprise-ready. Start selling to enterprise customers with just a few lines of code. Add Single Sign-On (and more) in minutes instead of months with WorkOS.
### But also
Datadog has been sponsoring the time of our lead maintainer for more than a year now. They also upgraded our account so that we can benefit from long-term telemetry (RFC).
SysGears also sponsored time from very early in the 2.x development. In particular, their strong investment is the reason why Yarn 2 supports node_modules installs even better than it used to.
Netlify has been the historical provider for our website. Each time we got issues, they jumped to our help. Their live previews have been super helpful in our development process.
Cloudflare has also been a historical partner. While we don't directly mirror the npm registry anymore, they still power our website to make its delivery as fast as possible.
Algolia contributed a lot to our documentation over the years. They still power the search engine we use on both versions of the documentation.
## Installation Consult the [Installation Guide](https://yarnpkg.com/getting-started/install). ## Migration Consult the [Migration Guide](https://yarnpkg.com/getting-started/migration). ## Documentation The documentation can be found at [yarnpkg.com](https://yarnpkg.com/). ## API The API documentation can be found at [yarnpkg.com/api](https://yarnpkg.com/api). ## Current status On top of our classic integration tests, we also run Yarn every day against the latest versions of the toolchains used by our community - just in case. report.overview: Berry is Yarn’s TypeScript package-manager monorepo, serving JavaScript developers, workspace maintainers, and tooling authors through both a CLI and reusable libraries. Its core manages dependency graphs, caches, installation state, and scripts, while plugins supply package protocols, commands, and filesystem installation strategies. The inspected implementation supports Plug’n’Play, node_modules, and pnpm-style linking, with a separate React/Docusaurus documentation application.
report.agent_prompt:
Onboard to yarnpkg/berry at commit e4e423a1eb117b5129f20ac626a03eb7a97aedff. Treat this brief as a bounded source investigation, not exhaustive coverage or proof that tests pass. Tests and CI definitions were inspected, not executed. Verify the checkout and relevant files before making drift-sensitive statements.

Start with package.json, packages/yarnpkg-cli/package.json, and packages/docusaurus/docs/advanced/04-technical/architecture.mdx. The root is a Yarn workspace monorepo. The CLI manifest declares version 4.18.1, while the root packageManager pins Yarn 4.2.1; these fields serve different purposes. Runtime support is Node >=18.12.0. Read tsconfig.json, eslint.config.mjs, and yarn.config.cjs before changing shared conventions or dependency declarations.

Trace startup through packages/yarnpkg-cli/sources/cli.ts, tools/getPluginConfiguration.ts, and lib.ts. runExit creates the Clipanion CLI; run validates Node, loads configuration, optionally delegates to yarnPath, handles cwd, registers plugin commands, and executes the parsed command. Configuration.find merges environment and RC settings, discovers the project, prepares the script environment, and activates bundled or dynamic plugins.

For install work, read plugin-essentials/sources/commands/install.ts and yarnpkg-core/sources/Project.ts. Keep reusable behavior in core or the responsible plugin because other commands also invoke Project.install. Follow validation, resolveEverything, fetchEverything, persist, linkEverything, and persistInstallStateFile. Immutable installs compare generated lockfile content before fetching. Update-lockfile mode limits fetching and skips linking. Resolution checking and lockfile refresh can be enabled by hardened mode.

For registry changes, inspect NpmSemverResolver, NpmSemverFetcher, npmHttpUtils, httpUtils, and Cache. Preserve candidate selection consistency between getCandidates and getSatisfying. Fetchers return filesystem handles and release callbacks. Cache validation precedes publication through temporary files and renames. Authentication and transport policy are centralized and configurable.

For execution changes, follow RunCommand into scriptUtils and yarnpkg-shell. Scripts precede dependency binaries; colon-named scripts can resolve across workspaces only when uniquely declared. Linkers own package locations. Dependency lifecycle builds have separate policy gates from explicit user script execution.

Prefer small changes in sources rather than generated bundles, hooks, workers, or grammars. Plugin interfaces expose commands, configuration, resolvers, fetchers, linkers, and ordered hooks. Read Installer.ts before changing filesystem ownership, custom state, or fetch-result lifetimes.

Under this investigation’s authority, use only read-only public-source commands prefixed with rtk proxy. Do not execute tests, install/build scripts, repository configuration, browsers, or network calls; do not read actual secrets or environment files. For a later authorized implementation, identify the smallest relevant Jest file or acceptance test first, then the repository lint and typecheck scripts. Report observed assertions, skipped cases, and execution results separately.

system_map.summary: The repository separates command dispatch, project management, protocol integrations, and filesystem installation. The CLI composes plugins around reusable core classes rather than containing the dependency engine itself. Distribution includes generated CLI bundles and published library packages, while documentation has its own application and build configuration.

claims.claim: The root package is a private packages/* workspace monorepo; it declares Jest, ESLint, and TypeScript scripts and pins packageManager to Yarn 4.2.1.
The executable source entrypoint imports polyfills and calls runExit with argv, portable cwd, its own path, and getPluginConfiguration().
lib.ts owns Clipanion context, Node >=18.12.0 validation, yarnPath delegation, plugin command registration, exit-code handling, and temporary-directory cleanup.
Core exposes Configuration, Project, Workspace, Cache, and Manifest; Project.find initializes resolutions and workspaces and uses linker lookup when cwd belongs to an installed package.
Plugin contributions are typed as configuration, commands, fetchers, linkers, resolvers, and hooks; the CLI’s standard bundle includes npm, JSR, constraints, linking, and workspace plugins.
Filesystem installation has distinct implementations: PnpLinker generates loader/data files, NodeModulesLinker persists a package tree, and plugin-pnpm registers PnpmLinker with a configurable store.

build:cli invokes builder build bundle, which bundles sources/cli.ts into bundles/yarn.js using esbuild; the manual release workflow builds binaries, pushes tags, and invokes release publishing scripts.
The separate Docusaurus workspace uses React 19 and provides development/build scripts; its configuration generates CLI and TypeDoc API documentation alongside docs and blog routes.

feature_catalog.summary: The inspected command registries cover dependency editing, installation, execution, diagnostics, workspace operations, and registry publishing. Protocol and linker plugins provide alternative dependency sources and installation layouts. Additional plugins support constraints, release workflows, patching, project creation, and editor tooling; this catalog groups the evidenced surfaces rather than asserting exhaustive inspection of every command implementation.

claims.claim: plugin-essentials registers add, remove, up, dedupe, install, rebuild, cache clean, resolution overrides, and package link/unlink commands.
Execution features include run, exec, and node; RunCommand supports top-level selection, binaries-only mode, Node --require forwarding, and a unique colon-named script fallback across workspaces.
Workspace features include listing and selecting a workspace, plus workspaces focus and foreach supplied by plugin-workspace-tools.

Installation supports PnP loader generation, a persisted node_modules tree, and a pnpm-style store; install also exposes immutable, immutable-cache, check-cache, refresh-lockfile, and execution modes.

Documented dependency integrations include npm semver, file, Git, GitHub, HTTP tarballs, exec, link, portal, and patch protocols; JSR adds its own resolver/fetcher and converts jsr: dependencies when packing.
npm CLI commands include audit, info, login/logout, publish, whoami, dist-tag management, and staged-publication approve/list/reject; publication provenance is a configurable option.

Constraints provide check/query/source commands and optional install-time checking; version provides apply/check/version with deferred records, while documented plugins add dlx, init, interactive upgrades, pack, patch, stage, and TypeScript assistance.

User diagnostics and tooling include config get/set/unset, explain and peer-requirement explanation, info, why, plugin management, Yarn version selection, PnPify, editor SDK generation, and a documentation site with CLI/configuration/API navigation.

data_flow.summary: Inputs enter through argv, environment settings, RC files, package manifests, and registry metadata. Configuration and Project own the interpreted settings and dependency graph, while fetchers translate package identities into filesystem-backed artifacts. Linkers publish runtime layouts, and lockfiles plus compressed installation state support subsequent commands.

claims.claim: argv becomes a Clipanion command after startup configuration and cwd handling; command context carries cwd, plugin configuration, and stdin/stdout/stderr.
Configuration.find combines environment settings, discovered RC files, and a home RC file; it processes yarnPath fields before project discovery and plugin activation.
Workspace.setup loads a manifest, derives stable workspace descriptors/locators from relative paths, expands workspace patterns, excludes node_modules/.git/.yarn, and sorts discovered paths.

Descriptor resolution first resolves resolver-specific dependencies, requests candidates, selects the first candidate, optionally verifies it with getSatisfying, and records descriptor-to-locator hashes.

NpmSemverResolver turns registry versions into approved, preferably nondeprecated candidates sorted descending; unconventional tarball URLs are bound into locators, and resolve loads manifest dependency metadata.
NpmSemverFetcher requests a checksum-aware cached package; a miss downloads a tarball and converts it into a vendor-prefixed ZIP, returning packageFs, releaseFs, prefixPath, and checksum.

fetchEverything updates storedChecksums and releases fetched filesystems; linkEverything creates installers with restored custom data, attaches internal/external relationships, and captures finalizeInstall custom data and build records.

Project.persist writes the normalized lockfile and workspace manifests; installation state is V8-serialized and gzipped, while restoration only reuses saved resolutions when the lockfile checksum matches.

behavior_traces.summary: Three concrete flows were followed through their implementation: CLI startup, installation through persistence, and script/binary execution. Startup can terminate by handing control to another Yarn executable. Installation and execution both restore project state, but apply different resolution, linking, and subprocess branches.

claims.claim: Startup: cli.ts calls getPluginConfiguration(), which reads the standard bundle list and constructs modules/plugins; runExit then calls getBaseCli() and run().

Startup dispatch: run() performs validateNodejsVersion → getCoreConfiguration → optional runYarnPath; otherwise checkCwd → initTelemetry → initCommands → cli.process → cli.run. Delegation sets YARN_IGNORE_PATH=1 in the child.

Install setup: InstallCommand.execute finds Project, applies applicable lockfile migration settings, finds Cache, requires a workspace, restores state without resolutions, and derives refresh/check behavior from explicit flags or hardened mode before Project.install.

Install resolution: Project.install runs validateProject, stops on validation errors, snapshots an immutable lockfile, invokes resolveEverything, emits peer warnings, and rejects changed generated lockfile content before fetching.

Install persistence: fetchEverything → optional persist → linkEverything → persistInstallStateFile → post-install validation. UpdateLockfile mode fetches only missing checksums and skips linking; SkipBuild returns from linking before package builds.

Run script: RunCommand.execute calls Configuration.find → Project.find → restoreInstallState → hasPackageScript → executePackageScript; initialization creates a temporary binary environment, then wrapScriptExecution wraps portable-shell execution.

Run fallback: absent a selected script, RunCommand checks dependency binaries and forwards Node flags; otherwise it accepts one matching colon-named workspace script. Binary execution chooses Node or direct pipevp and removes its binary folder in finally.

State recovery: restoreInstallState reads and gunzips the saved file, deserializes it, and restores requested categories. When resolution restoration is requested, unreadable state or a changed lockfile triggers applyLightResolution → resolveEverything(lockfileOnly) → persistInstallStateFile.

testing_signals.summary: Tests and CI were inspected, not executed; their existence is not a passing result. The sampled Jest suites exercise project recovery, configuration handling, installation modes, execution precedence, and mocked network behavior. CI defines broader platform and ecosystem checks, but this bounded investigation does not establish exhaustive coverage or current CI status.

claims.claim: Root test:unit uses Jest 29; its Node environment applies a custom JavaScript/TypeScript transformer and polyfills, excludes acceptance-tests and plugin-compat, and sets a 50-second timeout.

Acceptance tests have a separate Jest configuration and setup; beforeEach starts the package server and initializes the fixture registry, and test:integration delegates to test:unit with that configuration.
Project.test.ts asserts Manifest.raw updates, preservation of resolver-specific dependencies during lockfile-only resolution, and recovery after replacing installation state with invalid content.
Configuration.test.ts checks hideSecrets redaction for both top-level npmAuthToken and scoped tokens; this directly tests formatted access rather than every logging or subprocess exposure path.

Install acceptance assertions cover inline build logs, SkipBuild suppression without changing PnP artifacts, and immutable refusal to create or alter a lockfile; the inspected ZIP-symlink case excludes Windows.
Run acceptance tests cover invocation with and without run, script exit-code propagation, delegated yarnPath exit codes, dependency binary execution, and script precedence over binaries.

The inspected HTTP tests intercept requests through hooks: core checks wrapper arguments, while npm checks registry URL joining and noninteractive OTP failure. These tests do not themselves exercise real TLS, proxies, or live registry authentication.

Integration CI defines immutable/cache checks and sharded unit/acceptance jobs across Linux, Windows, and macOS; scheduled ecosystem workflows add compatibility checks, but the Webpack thread-loader case immediately exits and is not exercised.

risk_map.summary: These are security-sensitive source observations and one explicitly labeled review hypothesis, not confirmed vulnerabilities. The main boundaries involve dynamic code, inherited environments, authenticated network requests, archive integrity, and filesystem mutation. Persistence ordering and a documented symlink uncertainty also warrant care when changing critical flows.

claims.claim: Dynamic plugin loading executes dynamicRequire(pluginPath) and factory(pluginRequire); builtin modules remain available. Missing HTTP-sourced plugins are downloaded and written locally, with checksum enforcement conditional on a configured checksum.

Package lifecycle scripts can execute preinstall/install/postinstall or synthesized node-gyp rebuild; soft links, built metadata, enableScripts, and architecture gate these builds, while explicit run executes selected scripts through the shell.

Configuration reads a home RC file and configured environment files outside the immediate project boundary; makeScriptEnv copies the resulting environment into subprocess environments and prepends temporary wrappers to PATH.

Network policy is configurable: unsafe HTTP requires a hostname whitelist, enableNetwork can block requests, enableStrictSsl controls certificate rejection, and optional CA/certificate/key paths are read. npm authentication may supply hook headers, bearer tokens, Basic credentials, or OIDC tokens.

Archive mismatch handling depends on checksumBehavior: ignore preserves the expected hash, update accepts the actual hash, reset rejects the cached entry, and throw errors; check-cache overrides mismatch handling to throw, while linking requests skipIntegrityCheck.

Installation persists manifests/lockfile before linking and saves state before post-install validation; PnP finalization can remove detected node_modules or obsolete loader/unplugged artifacts, so failures can follow filesystem changes.

initializeWorkspaceEnvironment realpaths package.json to choose default cwd; its source comment explicitly says tests for that behavior are absent and the historical symlink use case is uncertain. This is a documented local coverage concern.

Review hypothesis: Smart merge crosses a consequential artifact trust boundary because pull_request_target checks out the PR head to generate a patch, then a separate job applies that artifact and pushes using a bot token. Exploitability was not assessed.

extension_points.summary: The Plugin type is the primary extension contract, with factories assembling runtime integrations. Typed configuration augmentation and ordered hooks allow cross-cutting behavior without expanding command implementations. Build profiles, shell builtins, and documentation plugins provide additional extension surfaces.

claims.claim: A Plugin can contribute configuration, command classes, fetchers, linkers, resolvers, and hooks; plugin-constraints demonstrates ConfigurationValueMap augmentation with typed settings and defaults.
CLI commands plug into each plugin’s commands array; initCommands iterates activated plugins and registers every contributed class with Clipanion.

Configuration.makeResolver constructs plugin resolver instances behind VirtualResolver and WorkspaceResolver; NpmSemverResolver demonstrates supportsDescriptor/supportsLocator, candidate selection, satisfying checks, and metadata resolution.
Configuration.makeFetcher composes builtin virtual/workspace fetchers with plugin fetchers; NpmSemverFetcher shows the cache loader pattern and filesystem/release/checksum result contract.

New installation layouts implement Linker package/location lookup and makeInstaller; Installer separates installPackage, dependency attachment, finalization, retained fetch lifetimes, and migratable custom state.

Hooks can modify script environments, wrap script/network execution, reduce dependency descriptors, and validate installs; triggerHook and reduceHook await contributors sequentially in plugin iteration order.
Builder supports additional --plugin entries and named profiles; findPlugins accepts profile combinations separated by '+', validates them against manifest bundles, and deduplicates contributions.

The portable shell accepts custom builtins, filesystem, environment, variables, and glob behavior; documentation extends separately through remark plugins, generated CLI docs, and TypeDoc entries discovered from package exports.

agent_handoff.summary: Begin with the relevant command, its core operation, and the owning plugin instead of treating this as a React application. Preserve generated-artifact boundaries, typed portable paths, and repository constraint conventions. Tests and CI were inspected, not executed; proposed checks below require separate execution authority, and the inventory remains bounded.

claims.claim: Read the root and CLI manifests first: CLI version 4.18.1 differs from the root packageManager pin of Yarn 4.2.1, and standard plugin membership is declared in the CLI manifest.

For installation changes, read InstallCommand and Project.install together; the command’s source explicitly directs reusable install customization into configuration/core because other commands also install projects.

For protocol changes, keep NpmSemverResolver.getCandidates and getSatisfying consistent: both use selectMatchingVersions, whose prerelease fallback applies only to a literal '*' with no stable matches.
For linker changes, honor Installer ordering and fetch-result ownership; custom data must tolerate absence and handle its own migration, and asynchronous holds require bounded concurrency.
Follow strict TypeScript and the portable-path conversions already used by Workspace; ESLint requires semverUtils.validRange and httpUtils instead of direct semver.Range/validRange and global fetch.

Dependency edits must account for yarn.config.cjs constraints: internal dependencies become workspace:^, most shared ranges are synchronized, lodash/inquirer are forbidden, and package metadata/prepack conventions are enforced.
Edit source implementations rather than generated bundles, hooks, workers, and grammars; ESLint excludes those outputs, while CI conditionally regenerates PnP hooks and checks their diffs.

Tests and CI were inspected, not executed. For later authorized validation, start with the affected Jest file or acceptance command suite using test:unit/test:integration, then use existing test:lint and typecheck:all scripts; mocked transport tests and explicitly skipped compatibility cases limit conclusions.
